name: Cibin Mathew Simon
headline: Full-stack Solution Architect · Cloud ERP & eCommerce · Java + Angular
headline_long: Full-stack Solution Architect designing and delivering cloud-based ERP and eCommerce platforms with Java and Angular, from first requirement to production.
summary: Full-stack Solution Architect with 8+ years at Rappit designing and delivering cloud-based ERP and eCommerce platforms with Java, Spring Boot and Angular on Google Cloud. Took a data-driven in-store commerce platform from first requirement to production in under six months, and led the migration of a ~20-application enterprise portfolio through a corporate demerger. Works directly with European stakeholders and stays hands-on across back end, data and cloud.
summary_full: Full-stack Solution Architect with 8+ years at Rappit, growing from developer to architect on cloud-based ERP and eCommerce platforms for European clients. I design back-end-heavy systems with Java, Spring Boot and Angular on Google Cloud, favouring pragmatic architecture: a modular monolith when speed to market matters, events at the seams, and data-driven designs that let the business change behaviour without a release. Recent work includes an in-store furniture commerce platform that went from first requirement to production in under six months, and the portfolio migration of ~20 enterprise applications through a corporate demerger.

projects.name: In-store furniture commerce platform
projects.context: An iPad progressive web app used by sales staff in the showroom to configure custom furniture with customers and sell it directly. It replaced a 1990s DOS-based configuration system and is live in 3 stores.
projects.team: Team of 8: technical architect (me), delivery manager, front-end lead, front-end developer, 3 full-stack developers, tester.
projects.stack: Java 21, Spring Boot, Angular PWA, PostgreSQL, Elasticsearch, Redis, BigQuery, Google Pub/Sub, Cloud Run, GitLab CI, Cloud Logging & Monitoring
bullets: Architected a data-driven platform on Java 21, Spring Boot, Angular PWA and GCP Cloud Run, from first requirement in Jun 2025 to production in Nov 2025, as a modular monolith (PIM + Sales: ordering, discounts, delivery, payments, contracts) built to split into microservices for a future warehouse and ERP phase.

Designed the data-driven product configurator and rule builder (guided flows and 2D drag-and-drop) that keeps every configuration consistent; 50+ suppliers onboarded, each with its own rule set, without code changes.
Introduced event-driven integration with Google Pub/Sub across modules, stock monitoring, BigQuery analytics and an AI service that converts supplier brochures into structured product data.
Cut product configuration time from ~60 min to 5–8 min; 100+ orders/day across 3 stores and growing; search under 500 ms with Elasticsearch.
Technical architect for a team of 8; 3-week sprints with weekly or biweekly rapid releases via GitLab CI; works directly with the client, including on-site visits to the Netherlands.
decisions: A data-driven platform had to reach production in about six months with a small team. Clear module boundaries (PIM, Sales) keep a later split into microservices open for the planned warehouse and ERP phase.
Products, options and validity rules live in data, not code, so new suppliers and product ranges go live without a release. Supports both guided flows and a 2D drag-and-drop builder.
Stock updates, analytics feeds and supplier imports are decoupled from the sales flow, so a slow consumer never blocks a sale in the store.
